entries.name: Mistake You Still Have to Put Right
entries.summary:
A mistake you made still has consequences that have not been repaired. The damage may be financial, social, professional, practical, or personal, but ignoring it has stopped being acceptable.

Narrative effects: You have learned to keep working toward a correction while paying close attention to the people and circumstances affected by what happened.

entries.name: Monster Attack Survivor
entries.summary:
You recently survived a genuine attack by a dangerous creature, leaving the reality of monsters much closer to your adult life than you expected.

Narrative effects: The attack taught you to act under fear and pay close attention to visible danger without automatically making you a trained monster hunter.

entries.name: Must Prove You Can Live Alone
entries.summary:
For the first time, you need to demonstrate that you can manage your own money, food, lodging, work, obligations, and decisions without another household quietly carrying you.

Narrative effects: Independent living has made consistent self-management and practical negotiation central adult skills.

entries.name: Need a Recommendation
entries.summary:
A job, academy, guild, post, contract, household, patron, or opportunity requires someone credible to speak for your character or competence.

Narrative effects: You have learned how much advancement can depend on persuading established people to attach their own reputation to yours.

entries.name: Need a Sponsor
entries.summary:
The next opportunity you want requires someone respected, wealthy, powerful, established, or connected enough to sponsor you.

Narrative effects: Seeking sponsorship has taught you to present your value convincingly while navigating formal relationships with people above your current position.

entries.name: Needed Money Fast
entries.summary:
An urgent expense forced you to find money quickly. The reason may have been practical, personal, medical, legal, professional, or otherwise pressing.

Narrative effects: Urgency taught you to ask who has work, money, credit, goods, or opportunities and what they expect in return.

entries.name: No One Is Coming to Fix It
entries.summary:
A problem in your life has reached the point where waiting for parents, patrons, authorities, employers, friends, or luck to solve it is no longer realistic.

Narrative effects: You have learned to continue acting even when responsibility is frightening and cannot be handed to someone else.

entries.name: Oath You Chose Yourself
entries.summary:
You deliberately committed yourself to an oath, principle, person, cause, duty, promise, or standard without someone else choosing it for you.

Narrative effects: A freely chosen commitment has become a source of personal discipline and something others may recognize in the way you act.

entries.name: Owe Someone a Favor
entries.summary:
Someone helped you when they did not have to, and the favor has become substantial enough that you know they may eventually ask something in return.

Narrative effects: You are highly aware of the personal obligations created by help and practiced at negotiating expectations within relationships.

entries.name: Partner Left You With the Work
entries.summary:
A business partner, coworker, sibling, companion, spouse, associate, or other person who shared important work has left, disappeared, withdrawn, or simply stopped carrying their part.

Narrative effects: Taking over abandoned responsibilities has required persistence and the ability to coordinate work that used to belong to more than one person.

entries.name: Personal Debt Comes Due
entries.summary:
A debt you personally accepted is now due, and delaying it further risks penalties, damaged reputation, legal consequences, repossession, or a creditor who has lost patience.

Narrative effects: Debt has made you attentive to terms, records, obligations, and the difference between what someone claims you owe and what the agreement actually says.

entries.name: Power Needs Restraint
entries.summary:
Your magical capabilities, or the consequences surrounding them, have made restraint increasingly important. Using power carelessly has become a problem you cannot ignore.

Narrative effects: You treat magical control as an adult responsibility. This trait applies only to magical capabilities the character genuinely possesses and grants no Arcana by itself.

entries.name: Promised Yourself You Would Leave
entries.summary:
You decided that your current town, household, job, institution, region, or way of life cannot be where you remain forever.

Narrative effects: You have begun thinking seriously about routes elsewhere and about the courage required to exchange familiarity for uncertainty.

entries.name: Promotion You Are Not Ready For
entries.summary:
You have been offered, assigned, or pushed toward more responsibility than you feel prepared to handle.

Narrative effects: Being pushed upward has forced you to make decisions for others while maintaining control over your own uncertainty.

entries.name: Mercenary Recruit
entries.summary:
You joined a mercenary band, sellsword company, caravan guard group, private retinue, or paid fighting force.

Narrative effects: You ask who is paying, who is lying, and who expects loyalty cheaper than death.

entries.name: Merchant Clerk
entries.summary:
You worked as a clerk, assistant, junior trader, shop hand, caravan bookkeeper, warehouse aide, or merchant house employee.

Narrative effects: You listen for profit, loss, shortage, and who is pretending not to be desperate.

entries.name: Merchant House Standing
entries.summary:
Your standing comes from trade, contracts, ownership, patronage, or a merchant house that expects profit and discretion.

Narrative effects: You hear family honor in coin, contract, reputation, ships, wagons, and whose seal backs a promise.

entries.name: Message Courier
entries.summary:
You carried messages between homes, halls, shrines, shops, nobles, camps, or distant settlements. Trust and speed mattered more than your age.

Narrative effects: You ask who needs to know, who must not know, and how fast the message must move.

entries.name: Militia Regular
entries.summary:
You remained a civilian, but local militia service became a normal part of adult life. Drills, watches, musters, patrols, weapons checks, alarm plans, and being expected to stand with neighbors under threat were recurring responsibilities.

Narrative effects: You think about defense in terms of ordinary people, limited equipment, familiar ground, and how quickly a peaceful place can need armed hands.

entries.name: Mill Worker
entries.summary:
You worked in or around a grain mill, sawmill, watermill, windmill, press, or similar working machinery. Loads, gears, belts, wheels, jams, maintenance, sacks, dust, water, and heavy moving parts shaped the work.

Narrative effects: You listen to working machinery closely enough to notice when its ordinary rhythm changes.

entries.name: Minor Noble Debut
entries.summary:
You made your first formal appearance as a young noble, house representative, court hopeful, heir, ward, or marriage prospect.

Narrative effects: You remember the first room where everyone measured whether you mattered.

entries.name: Monster Handler's Assistant
entries.summary:
You assisted someone who captured, studied, transported, guarded, healed, or controlled dangerous beasts and monster-like creatures. You learned that fear is useful, but panic is not.

Narrative effects: You ask what a creature understands before asking how dangerous it is.

entries.name: Never Found Your Trade
entries.summary:
You have worked and tried to be useful, but no profession ever became clearly yours. Perhaps you tried several apprenticeships, never had the money or sponsorship for one, lost interest, lacked opportunity, or simply reached adulthood before finding a path that fit.

Narrative effects: You recognize how quickly temporary work can become a life if nobody chooses a different direction.

entries.name: New Soldier
entries.summary:
You entered military service, guard work, militia duty, mercenary training, or organized martial life as a young adult.

Narrative effects: You check gear, formation, exits, and who is hiding fear behind discipline.

entries.name: Newly Independent
entries.summary:
You recently began living as your own person, separate from the household, village, institution, or family structure that shaped you. Freedom came with rent, hunger, choices, mistakes, and the strange realization that no one else would automatically solve your problems.

Narrative effects: You keep track of coin, food, shelter, and obligations more carefully than you used to.

entries.name: Noble Living Quietly
entries.summary:
You are noble-born, noble-connected, or secretly high-status, but began adult life quietly, hidden, disguised, exiled, protected, or far from courtly attention.

Narrative effects: You know how to hide rank in habits that keep trying to reveal it.

entries.name: Ordinary Life Interrupted
entries.summary:
Your early adult life was ordinary until something broke it: summons, death, attack, prophecy, inheritance, monster, magic, scandal, exile, or a stranger at the wrong door.

Narrative effects: You remember the exact moment ordinary stopped being available.

entries.name: Palace Staffer
entries.summary:
You served in a palace, noble estate, royal residence, temple court, or high household during early adulthood. Formality, service routes, schedules, and quiet information shaped your daily life.

Narrative effects: You can tell when a grand household is functioning by listening to the servants, not the nobles.

entries.name: Performer on the Road
entries.summary:
You traveled as a performer: singer, dancer, actor, storyteller, acrobat, musician, comic, stage hand, or spectacle worker. Applause and hunger both followed the road.

Narrative effects: You read a crowd by hunger, mood, coin, boredom, and how close the guards are standing.

entries.name: Property Caretaker
entries.summary:
You looked after a building, shrine, workshop, storehouse, abandoned property, small estate, grounds, animals, or other place whose owner expected it to remain usable. Much of the work was maintenance nobody noticed unless it was neglected.

Narrative effects: You notice small maintenance problems while they are still cheaper and easier than emergencies.

entries.name: Made Up Stories
entries.summary:
You invented adventures, heroes, villains, kingdoms, monsters, family dramas, ridiculous lies, or elaborate imaginary histories simply because creating stories was fun.

Narrative effects: You find it easy to shape events into narratives and present ideas in ways that hold attention.

entries.name: Mana Flickered Around You
entries.summary:
Minor magical disturbances occasionally occurred around you during childhood: lights flickered, objects shifted, sparks appeared, mana reacted strangely, or adults noticed brief incidents that suggested magical sensitivity without clear control.

Narrative effects: You learned early that emotional control and attention can matter around unstable mana. This trait does not grant a specific Arcana.

entries.name: Mediated Other Children
entries.summary:
When other children argued, you often became the one trying to make both sides stop shouting long enough to solve the problem. Sometimes they even listened.

Narrative effects: You naturally listen for what each side actually wants before trying to persuade them toward a compromise.

entries.name: Mocked for Strange Blood
entries.summary:
Other children or adults mocked, excluded, questioned, or stared at you because of ancestry, visible traits, mixed heritage, rumored parentage, or assumptions about what kind of people you came from.

Narrative effects: You understand the sting of being reduced to ancestry and are sensitive to similar treatment directed at others.

entries.name: Monster-Touched Childhood
entries.summary:
A monster, dangerous creature, magical beast, or unnatural presence became part of a memorable childhood event. You may have seen it, survived it, been rescued from it, or simply lived somewhere its presence affected daily life.

Narrative effects: Unusual creatures do not feel entirely abstract to you, but one childhood encounter did not make you a professional monster hunter.

entries.name: Never Liked Crowds
entries.summary:
Festivals, packed markets, ceremonies, busy halls, and noisy gatherings exhausted or unsettled you. You preferred edges, side rooms, rooftops, quiet streets, or smaller groups.

Narrative effects: In crowded spaces you instinctively look for quieter positions where you can reduce attention and separate useful sounds from the surrounding noise.

entries.name: Never Where Expected
entries.summary:
Adults repeatedly discovered that you had slipped away from the place they thought you were. You wandered through buildings, gardens, streets, fields, or neighboring properties with an inconvenient talent for avoiding notice.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable moving independently through familiar environments without announcing every departure.

entries.name: Ordinary Happy Childhood
entries.summary:
Nothing singularly tragic, mysterious, prestigious, magical, or dramatic defined these years. You played, learned ordinary things, knew familiar people, had good and bad days, and generally remember childhood as a happy part of your life.

Narrative effects: You possess a grounded sense of ordinary community life and healthy familiarity with everyday relationships. Do not invent a hidden childhood tragedy, prophecy, bloodline, or secret event simply because the character later becomes important.

entries.name: Played at Being a Knight
entries.summary:
You repeatedly played at being a knight, guard, champion, duelist, or heroic warrior. Sticks became swords, blankets became cloaks, and other children were recruited as allies, rivals, or unfortunate villains.

Narrative effects: Childhood imitation gave you familiarity with martial ideas and a rudimentary sense of distance and timing, but not professional combat training.

entries.name: Played at Being a Mage
entries.summary:
You copied gestures, invented spells, drew meaningless circles, collected interesting sticks as staves, declared ordinary stones enchanted, and pretended to perform magic long before any real magical training.

Narrative effects: You recognize common magical imagery and behavior from years of imitation, but this trait does not grant actual spellcasting or an Arcana.

entries.name: Praised for Strange Talent
entries.summary:
Adults repeatedly praised you for some unusual knack, striking instinct, unusual memory, captivating manner, peculiar perception, or other talent that seemed remarkable for a child.

Narrative effects: Being noticed for talent made you comfortable with attention and with demonstrating something when others expect you to impress them. The exact childhood talent remains part of the character's established history.

entries.name: Prize Pupil
entries.summary:
Teachers regularly considered you one of the strongest pupils in your lessons. Good marks, remembered answers, neat work, or unusual consistency earned you praise and raised expectations.

Narrative effects: Formal learning feels familiar, and you are practiced at turning information into clear written work rather than merely memorizing it.

entries.name: Protected the Weak
entries.summary:
Even as a child, you repeatedly stepped between stronger children and someone smaller, younger, isolated, frightened, or unable to defend themselves.

Narrative effects: When a group hesitates while someone vulnerable needs help, you have an old instinct to act and encourage others to follow.

entries.name: Market Child
entries.summary:
You spent much of childhood in markets, squares, stalls, loading areas, food rows, auction yards, or other crowded spaces where goods and people constantly changed hands.

Narrative effects: Prices, negotiation, public conversation, and the flow of local information through commercial spaces feel familiar.

entries.name: Millhouse Child
entries.summary:
You spent childhood around a mill where gears, stones, belts, wheels, grain, sacks, flour, water, wind, noise, and heavy work were everyday sights.

Narrative effects: Simple mechanical systems and the physical realities of moving heavy materials feel familiar.

entries.name: Mine Camp Child
entries.summary:
Mine entrances, lifts, support timbers, carts, bells, machinery, workers, dust, ore, and conversations about tunnel safety formed much of your childhood environment.

Narrative effects: Mechanical and structural sounds catch your attention, especially in enclosed working environments.

entries.name: Mountain Hold Child
entries.summary:
Steep paths, stairs, cliff roads, high walls, exposed walkways, cold weather, and elevation shaped your childhood movement through home.

Narrative effects: Vertical terrain feels natural, and physical exposure to cold, wind, and elevation bothers you less than it otherwise might.

entries.name: Noble Among Commoner Children
entries.summary:
Your birth, family, or legal status placed you above most of the children you spent time with, but your actual playmates and companions were largely common-born.

Narrative effects: You are familiar with ordinary community habits and with navigating moments when your formal position gives your words more weight than your friendships suggest.

entries.name: Noble Etiquette Lessons
entries.summary:
A meaningful part of childhood involved formal instruction in greetings, precedence, dining, introductions, posture, titles, noble houses, and the expected behavior of respectable society.

Narrative effects: Formal manners and noble symbols feel learned rather than mysterious, though this does not itself establish noble birth.

entries.name: Noble Playmate
entries.summary:
You were a regular childhood companion to one or more noble children. Games, lessons, arguments, favors, secrets, and social boundaries made rank something personal rather than abstract.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable interacting informally with high-status people while still recognizing when formality suddenly matters.

entries.name: Orchard Child
entries.summary:
Fruit trees, vines, groves, harvest baskets, pruning, windfalls, storage sheds, preserving, and seasonal changes shaped the places where you played and helped.

Narrative effects: Cultivated plants and the preparation or preservation of their harvest feel familiar.

entries.name: Pilgrim Road Child
entries.summary:
Pilgrim routes, shrines, roadside chapels, hostels, holy destinations, religious travelers, and repeated stories of distant sacred places shaped your childhood surroundings.

Narrative effects: You understand how faith and travel intersect and are familiar with the routes and landmarks that grow around pilgrimage.

entries.name: Protected by One Kind Adult
entries.summary:
Whatever else childhood was like, one adult repeatedly made sure you had somewhere safer to stand. They may have been family, a neighbor, worker, teacher, guard, servant, priest, or someone with no formal obligation to you.

Narrative effects: You recognize the importance of a single reliable person in an otherwise uncertain environment and are sensitive to others who need the same.

entries.name: Martial Artist
entries.summary:
You specialize in disciplined unarmed technique built around stance, timing, combinations, counters, redirection, footwork, breathing, and precise body control. Your training emphasizes efficiency and technical execution over brute force.

Narrative effects: You habitually adjust stance, balance, and distance, treating the whole body as a coordinated fighting tool rather than a collection of separate attacks.

entries.name: Mobile Marksman
entries.summary:
You specialize in maintaining ranged effectiveness while moving, changing position, finding new angles, and shooting without relying on one perfect stationary firing point. Your discipline blends bow work with agile battlefield movement.

Narrative effects: You constantly search for the next shooting angle, keeping movement and line of sight connected rather than treating marksmanship as a stationary task.

entries.name: Mounted Combatant
entries.summary:
You are trained to fight while mounted, coordinating balance, weapon handling, the mount's movement, and changing ground under combat pressure. Your expertise applies to ordinary and unusual mounts without granting mastery over every creature you might ride.

Narrative effects: You read open ground in terms of approach lines, turning space, momentum, and what a mount can safely do while weapons are in use.

entries.name: Polearm Specialist
entries.summary:
You specialize in long battlefield weapons such as halberds, glaives, poleaxes, and similar polearms. Your training emphasizes reach, lane control, sweeping attacks, hooks, formation spacing, and changing grips as enemies move through different distances.

Narrative effects: You see combat in lanes and distances, instinctively considering where a long weapon can deny movement, support a line, or punish an approach.

entries.name: Magnetic Presence
entries.summary:
You naturally project confidence, personality, authority, or social energy strongly enough to hold attention and shape a room. Grants +8 Communication.

Narrative effects: You make eye contact, speak with deliberate emphasis, and instinctively adjust your delivery to keep other people engaged.

entries.name: Martial Power
entries.summary:
You combine physical power, leverage, and force with close-combat timing, pressure, defense, and weapon exchanges in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Strength and +4 Fighting.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing physical power, leverage, and force and close-combat timing, pressure, defense, and weapon exchanges together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Martial Precision
entries.summary:
Your combat aptitude strongly favors close engagement, while controlled accuracy supports the openings you create. Grants +6 Fighting and +2 Accuracy.

Narrative effects: You usually lead with close-combat timing, pressure, defense, and weapon exchanges, calling on aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement to support that strength when the situation demands it.

entries.name: Methodical Power
entries.summary:
You combine physical power, leverage, and force with memory, structured reasoning, theory, and technical understanding in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Strength and +4 Intelligence.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing physical power, leverage, and force and memory, structured reasoning, theory, and technical understanding together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Mobile Fighter
entries.summary:
Your aptitude strongly favors agility, balance, speed, and bodily control, while close-combat timing, pressure, defense, and weapon exchanges provides a meaningful secondary strength. Grants +6 Dexterity and +2 Fighting.

Narrative effects: You usually lead with agility, balance, speed, and bodily control, calling on close-combat timing, pressure, defense, and weapon exchanges to support that strength when the situation demands it.

entries.name: Observant Reasoning
entries.summary:
You balance structured reasoning with close observation and pattern recognition. Grants +4 Intelligence and +4 Perception.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing memory, structured reasoning, theory, and technical understanding and awareness, observation, pattern recognition, and subtle cues together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Ordered Mind
entries.summary:
You combine memory, structured reasoning, theory, and technical understanding with resolve, focus, emotional control, and resistance to pressure in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Intelligence and +4 Willpower.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing memory, structured reasoning, theory, and technical understanding and resolve, focus, emotional control, and resistance to pressure together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Perceptive Aim
entries.summary:
You combine aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement with awareness, observation, pattern recognition, and subtle cues in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Accuracy and +4 Perception.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement and awareness, observation, pattern recognition, and subtle cues together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Persuasive Resolve
entries.summary:
Your aptitude strongly favors outward influence, supported by enough inner resolve to keep your footing when challenged or dismissed. Grants +6 Communication and +2 Willpower.

Narrative effects: You usually lead with presence, expression, persuasion, and social projection, calling on resolve, focus, emotional control, and resistance to pressure to support that strength when the situation demands it.

entries.name: Physical Discipline
entries.summary:
Your aptitude strongly favors endurance, resilience, recovery, and resistance to strain, while resolve, focus, emotional control, and resistance to pressure provides a meaningful secondary strength. Grants +6 Constitution and +2 Willpower.

Narrative effects: You usually lead with endurance, resilience, recovery, and resistance to strain, calling on resolve, focus, emotional control, and resistance to pressure to support that strength when the situation demands it.

entries.name: Powerful Frame
entries.summary:
Your natural build strongly favors leverage, force, and direct physical power. Grants +8 Strength.

Narrative effects: You approach physical obstacles through leverage and committed force, but your movement remains controlled rather than reckless.

entries.name: Master Craft Line
entries.summary:
Your family has built its reputation through generations of skilled craft rather than rank or conquest. The exact craft may vary, but the family name carries expectations of careful hands, good materials, professional pride, and work worth paying for.

Narrative effects: You judge reputation through workmanship and notice when someone is paying for genuine quality, fashionable appearance, or a famous maker's name.

entries.name: Merchant Dynasty
entries.summary:
Generations of your family built wealth and reputation through trade, contracts, ships, caravans, warehouses, brokerage, or commercial relationships. The family name may open doors because people remember profitable dealings, reliable delivery, old debts, or expensive disputes.

Narrative effects: You instinctively consider what a relationship is worth, what it costs to damage it, and whether today's bargain will still matter years from now.

entries.name: Midwife Tradition
entries.summary:
Midwives, birth attendants, postpartum caregivers, or other people trusted during pregnancy and childbirth recur through your family history. Family stories remember difficult nights, frightened households, practical care, and the quiet responsibility of being present when lives begin.

Narrative effects: You treat childbirth and caregiving as practical human realities and pay attention to both physical needs and the fear or exhaustion surrounding them.

entries.name: Military Family
entries.summary:
Soldiers, guards, officers, militia leaders, mercenaries, or other martial professionals recur throughout your family history. Campaign stories, old wounds, discipline, equipment, duty, and arguments about command became part of the family's ordinary language.

Narrative effects: You notice whether authority is backed by preparation, discipline, supplies, and people willing to follow when danger becomes real.

entries.name: Miller's Family
entries.summary:
Millers recur through your family history, working around gears, stones, wheels, belts, water, wind, grain, heavy sacks, and machinery that could feed a community or injure someone careless. A working mill was both livelihood and mechanism.

Narrative effects: You recognize common mechanical principles in mills and understand the physical labor required to keep material moving through them.

entries.name: Miner Family
entries.summary:
Miners, pit workers, tunnel crews, prospectors, ore sorters, or underground laborers recur through your family history. Supports, ventilation, seams, darkness, collapses, hidden pockets, and the constant search for worthwhile material shaped the family tradition.

Narrative effects: You pay attention to constructed supports and concealed signs of useful or dangerous material in places where poor observation can become deadly.

entries.name: Mixed-Tradition Family
entries.summary:
Your family combines different cultural, regional, professional, religious, social, or household traditions rather than presenting one simple inherited identity. Different relatives may tell different stories about what the family really is.

Narrative effects: You are accustomed to moving between overlapping family traditions and to noticing how people negotiate identity when more than one background is genuinely theirs.

entries.name: Newly Raised House
entries.summary:
Your family entered the nobility only recently through achievement, wealth, marriage, service, royal favor, military distinction, or another accepted path upward. The title may be real, but older families have not forgotten how recently your ancestors stood outside their circle.

Narrative effects: You notice when old elites politely test whether your family has learned the rules quickly enough to deserve its new place.

entries.name: Old Noble Line
entries.summary:
Your family has held noble standing for generations, accumulating traditions, marriages, obligations, rivalries, and a name that carries weight in the circles where it is known. The line is old and established without being one of the Firstblood Houses.

Narrative effects: You understand that an old family name carries remembered favors, grudges, expectations, and comparisons to relatives you may never have met.

entries.name: Potter's Line
entries.summary:
Potters, tile makers, ceramic workers, kiln workers, or other clay craftspeople recur through your family history. Clay quality, moisture, shape, drying, firing, breakage, and the feel of material under the hands became part of family knowledge.

Narrative effects: You are familiar with clay work and instinctively pay attention to texture, moisture, surface flaws, and other details best understood through touch.

entries.name: Material Scholar
entries.summary:
You specialize in the properties, quality, uses, weaknesses, sourcing, and identification of physical materials such as metals, stone, timber, glass, ceramics, fibers, and composites. Unlike a general Appraiser, your interest is how materials behave and what they are suited to do.

Narrative effects: You pay attention to composition, grain, hardness, brittleness, wear, joins, treatment, and whether the material is appropriate for the job it is being asked to perform.

entries.name: Medic
entries.summary:
You have substantial knowledge of anatomy, wounds, illness, disease, poison symptoms, first aid, recovery, exhaustion, hygiene, and nonmagical treatment. This focus represents medical expertise and does not grant Healing Arcana or any supernatural healing ability.

Narrative effects: You watch breathing, bleeding, temperature, pain, movement, symptoms, and likely causes before deciding what treatment or further examination is appropriate.

entries.name: Military Scholar
entries.summary:
You have studied warfare, formations, command structures, fortifications, logistics, campaigns, doctrine, military institutions, and the lessons preserved from earlier conflicts. This is knowledge of warfare rather than automatic skill with weapons or authority over soldiers.

Narrative effects: You read a military situation through supply, terrain, command, formation, fortification, precedent, and what an army appears to be preparing to do.

entries.name: Monster Scholar
entries.summary:
You study dangerous creatures through anatomy, behavior, feeding, habitat, breeding, territorial signs, vulnerabilities, and ecological relationships. This focus is strongest for creatures that can be understood as living beings or manifested fauna rather than every supernatural phenomenon being treated as the same kind of monster.

Narrative effects: You begin with tracks, remains, habitat, feeding signs, movement, and behavior before deciding what sort of creature is responsible.

entries.name: Musicologist
entries.summary:
You study musical traditions, instruments, forms, ceremonial music, performance conventions, famous works, regional styles, and the cultural meanings carried through music. This is musical knowledge rather than automatic talent as a performer.

Narrative effects: You recognize style, instrument, tradition, ceremonial purpose, regional influence, and the cultural references hidden inside a piece of music.

entries.name: Naturalist
entries.summary:
You study living systems: animals, plants, fungi, weather, terrain, habitats, ecological relationships, natural hazards, and the ways organisms survive in their environments. Your knowledge is broader than tracking one creature and does not automatically include magical monster lore.

Narrative effects: You read terrain and living things as an interconnected system, noticing what belongs, what is stressed, what is dangerous, and what recent change may have disturbed the environment.

entries.name: Planar Scholar
entries.summary:
You specialize in planes, dimensional boundaries, spatial anomalies, otherworldly environments, crossings, extraplanar entities, and places whose rules differ from ordinary geography. Your knowledge helps interpret planar phenomena without making every strange event planar by default.

Narrative effects: You become alert around impossible distances, repeated spaces, wrong boundaries, unusual crossings, and evidence that a place may not obey normal spatial rules.

entries.name: Political Scholar
entries.summary:
You have studied governments, offices, legitimacy, civic institutions, succession systems, taxation, administration, diplomacy, political customs, and the ways states distribute authority. You understand political structures without automatically knowing every private faction plan inside them.

Narrative effects: You ask which office holds authority, how that authority is recognized, what institutions support it, and where formal government ends and political influence begins.

entries.name: Metal Arcana
entries.summary:
You have a natural gift for Metal Arcana: metal, alloy, ore, forged objects, metal resonance, and worked arms or armor. Your magic expresses this theme instinctively, and training turns that instinct into controlled spellwork.

Narrative effects: You notice ringing steel, stressed hinges, hidden nails, and the weight of worked metal.

entries.name: Motion Arcana
entries.summary:
You have a natural gift for Motion Arcana: movement, momentum, acceleration, deceleration, balance, impact rhythm, and kinetic flow. Your magic expresses this theme instinctively, and training turns that instinct into controlled spellwork.

Narrative effects: You notice rhythm, balance, acceleration, and the moment movement wants to change direction.

entries.name: Poison Arcana
entries.summary:
You have a natural gift for Poison Arcana: toxins, venoms, irritants, antidotal reactions, contamination, and bodily resistance to poison. Your magic expresses this theme instinctively, and training turns that instinct into controlled spellwork.

Narrative effects: You notice bitter scents, tainted cups, venomous colors, and the way bodies react to hidden toxins.

entries.name: Power Arcana
entries.summary:
You have a natural gift for Power Arcana: amplification, reinforcement, body-strengthening, magical pressure, and turning raw force into directed action.

Narrative effects: Occasionally break things you are not trying to break when under stress.

entries.name: Protection Arcana
entries.summary: You have a natural gift for Protection Arcana: wards, shields, barriers, resistance, guarded thresholds, and power shaped to preserve rather than destroy.

entries.name: Nightglass Courtwise
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Nightglass court culture, where vampire houses, protected communities, invitations, sanctuary law, elegant manners, and predatory interests coexist behind polished behavior. Shadow magic is a characteristic cultural art because concealment, controlled darkness, and what remains unseen are politically meaningful.

Narrative effects: You read formal behavior and the feelings beneath it with care. Shadow Arcana reflects Nightglass cultural magic without implying that you are a vampire, courtier, or predator.

entries.name: Nightglass Sanctuary-Bred
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Nightglass sanctuary law, protected communities, old bargains, negotiated coexistence, and the social networks required for ordinary people to live beside powerful predatory houses. Shadow magic remains part of the culture, but here it is familiar as environment and custom rather than courtly display.

Narrative effects: You understand Nightglass agreements, protections, reputations, and the people who make local arrangements actually function. Shadow Arcana reflects the culture around you without defining your social class.
