You have deliberately learned to combine Bargaining and Faction Lore as one working discipline instead of treating them as unrelated skills. The overlap gives you options that depend on both kinds of competence and grants the signature ability Trade the Pressure.

Narrative effects: Treat Political Negotiator as a genuine hybrid specialization. The character combines Bargaining with Faction Lore when both materially matter to the approach; do not let either skill substitute for the other or bypass normal tools, authority, resources, evidence, positioning, or consequences.

facts.label: Requirements
facts.value: characterLevel 10, Bargaining skill 30, Faction Lore skill 30

entries.name: Power Arcana Mastery
entries.summary:
You have trained Power Arcana beyond simple affinity into a major specialization. Your control is more precise, economical, and reliable inside its established domain, but mastery does not expand what the Arcana governs or remove mana costs, opposition, risk, or story consequences. This mastery grants the signature ability Perfect Reinforcement.

Narrative effects: Treat Power Arcana as a major specialization. Favor deliberate, technically informed expressions of the authored Power Arcana domain; do not reinterpret it as another Arcana, grant effects outside its definition, or waive normal mana, strain, witnesses, and consequences. The character may use Perfect Reinforcement when its fictional setup is plausible; it is a mastery technique, not automatic success or permission to exceed the Arcana domain.

entries.name: Protection Arcana Mastery
entries.summary:
You have trained Protection Arcana beyond simple affinity into a major specialization. Your control is more precise, economical, and reliable inside its established domain, but mastery does not expand what the Arcana governs or remove mana costs, opposition, risk, or story consequences. This mastery grants the signature ability All-Angle Guard.

Narrative effects: Treat Protection Arcana as a major specialization. Favor deliberate, technically informed expressions of the authored Protection Arcana domain; do not reinterpret it as another Arcana, grant effects outside its definition, or waive normal mana, strain, witnesses, and consequences. The character may use All-Angle Guard when its fictional setup is plausible; it is a mastery technique, not automatic success or permission to exceed the Arcana domain.

entries.name: Public Advocate
entries.summary:
You have deliberately learned to combine Persuasion and Cultural Lore as one working discipline instead of treating them as unrelated skills. The overlap gives you options that depend on both kinds of competence and grants the signature ability Put It on the Record.

Narrative effects: Treat Public Advocate as a genuine hybrid specialization. The character combines Persuasion with Cultural Lore when both materially matter to the approach; do not let either skill substitute for the other or bypass normal tools, authority, resources, evidence, positioning, or consequences.

facts.label: Requirements
facts.value: characterLevel 10, Persuasion skill 30, Cultural Lore skill 30

entries.name: Map Copyist
entries.summary:
You were regularly expected to copy route maps, property plans, simple charts, boundaries, or geographic notes carefully enough that others could use them.

Narrative effects: Representing space accurately and producing careful mundane lines and labels became repeated work.

entries.name: Market Apprentice
entries.summary:
You assisted a vendor or trader with stock, prices, customers, displays, deliveries, and simple negotiation without yet being responsible for the business yourself.

Narrative effects: Negotiating ordinary exchanges and judging physical goods became repeated practical responsibilities.

entries.name: Market Stall Helper
entries.summary:
You helped run a stall by arranging goods, answering customers, watching stock, carrying purchases, and participating in simple negotiations.

Narrative effects: Prices, customer negotiation, physical goods, and basic judgments of quality became routine.

entries.name: Miller's Helper
entries.summary:
You moved grain, sacks, tools, and finished meal around a working mill and helped with simple tasks surrounding its machinery.

Narrative effects: Basic mill mechanisms and the physical work surrounding them are familiar.

entries.name: Mine Lamp Bearer
entries.summary:
You carried lamps, tools, messages, or small supplies through mine workings and learned to listen closely to machinery, supports, echoes, and warnings from deeper tunnels.

Narrative effects: Enclosed constructed spaces make you attentive to mechanical and structural sounds.

entries.name: Monastery Novice
entries.summary:
You were expected to follow a monastery's routines: simple work, lessons, silence, prayer, cleaning, memorization, or other disciplined communal duties.

Narrative effects: Structured religious routine and disciplined repetition feel familiar regardless of your later beliefs.

entries.name: Mountain Pass Runner
entries.summary:
You carried messages or small loads across steep local paths, stairs, ridges, or mountain routes where careless footing could cost valuable time.

Narrative effects: Steep routes and vertical terrain feel practical rather than exceptional.

entries.name: Noble Tutor's Student
entries.summary:
A tutor expected regular study from you in letters, histories, conduct, arithmetic, languages, or other respectable subjects associated with formal education.

Narrative effects: Structured written study and historical instruction feel familiar without this trait requiring noble birth.

entries.name: Nomad Trail Child
entries.summary:
You were expected to contribute during regular migration or travel by helping with mounts, route awareness, packing, camps, and keeping pace with the moving community.

Narrative effects: Mounted travel and route-finding are familiar parts of ordinary movement rather than inherently military skills.

entries.name: Orchard Picker
entries.summary:
Seasonal picking, sorting, carrying baskets, climbing for fruit, and identifying what was ready became a regular part of your preteen work.

Narrative effects: Cultivated plants and moving safely among trees feel familiar from repeated seasonal work.

entries.name: Potter's Helper
entries.summary:
You prepared clay, moved finished pieces, cleaned tools, helped with simple shaping, and learned how moisture, pressure, and texture changed the material.

Narrative effects: You are practiced at judging physical materials through touch and shaping them carefully by hand.

entries.name: Magic Came Too Easily
entries.summary:
Early magical exercises seemed easier for you than expected. Praise, jealousy, concern, or overconfidence followed, and you learned that natural aptitude still needed control.

Narrative effects: You understand magical concepts readily but learned that talent without control can become dangerous. This trait grants no Arcana by itself.

entries.name: Magic Frightened You
entries.summary:
A magical event frightened you badly enough that you had to decide whether to avoid magic forever or learn enough about it to stop feeling helpless.

Narrative effects: Magical danger still commands your respect, but fear taught you to understand rather than simply recoil from it.

entries.name: Mana Control Drills
entries.summary:
You spent part of your preteen years practicing controlled breathing, concentration, repetition, and other exercises intended to keep magical energy stable.

Narrative effects: You associate safe magical practice with patience and control rather than raw enthusiasm. This trait does not grant a specific Arcana.

entries.name: Met a Foreign Traveler
entries.summary:
A traveler from a culture meaningfully different from your own spent enough time speaking with you that distant customs stopped feeling entirely imaginary.

Narrative effects: The encounter taught you to ask how unfamiliar customs work instead of assuming your own are universal.

entries.name: Promise Made to a Dying Adult
entries.summary:
An adult who expected to die asked something of you, and you gave your word. The promise may have been simple, impossible, fulfilled long ago, or still unresolved.

Narrative effects: You understand the emotional gravity of promises made when someone believes they have little time left. The trait does not dictate whether the promise still binds you.

entries.name: Protected Someone From Punishment
entries.summary:
You intervened when someone else faced punishment, accusation, or retaliation, arguing for them, accepting some responsibility, or persuading an authority to reconsider.

Narrative effects: You learned how advocacy can change what happens to another person and how stepping forward can influence a group.

entries.name: Mason
entries.summary:
You are professionally experienced in building and repairing with stone, brick, mortar, foundations, walls, arches, paving, and other structural masonry. You understand fit, load, settlement, drainage, and how small construction mistakes become large failures.

Narrative effects: You inspect courses, joints, cracks, foundations, drainage, load paths, and tool marks before deciding whether masonry is sound, failing, or hiding later alterations.

entries.name: Merchant
entries.summary:
You are experienced in buying, selling, pricing, negotiating, moving, and evaluating goods in practical markets. You understand demand, scarcity, quality, tariffs, trade customs, merchant relationships, and the difference between theoretical value and what someone will actually pay.

Narrative effects: You listen for scarcity, urgency, transport risk, quality problems, hidden costs, and the moment either side reveals what matters more to them than the stated price.

entries.name: Miller
entries.summary:
You are professionally experienced in operating and maintaining milling work that turns grain or other raw material into usable product. You understand grind, feed rate, wear, storage, contamination, quality, and the practical machinery or tools involved in the work.

Narrative effects: You inspect grain, grind, dust, wear, storage, sound, and the condition of the working surfaces before trusting the quality or safety of a mill's output.

entries.name: Miner
entries.summary:
You are professionally experienced in extracting useful material underground or from exposed workings. You understand rock, ore signs, basic supports, ventilation concerns, tunnel hazards, work faces, hauling, and the practical difference between promising stone and dangerous ground.

Narrative effects: You watch fractures, dust, damp, supports, roof shape, ore traces, and how sound travels through stone before trusting an underground space.

entries.name: Navigator
entries.summary:
You are professionally trained to determine position and direction using landmarks, stars, instruments, charts, roads, coastlines, currents, terrain, and other reliable references. Your navigation can support travel by land, sea, river, or other environments where maintaining a known course matters.

Narrative effects: You continually compare heading, distance, landmarks, weather, charts, and prior position so that small errors are corrected before they become being lost.

entries.name: Palace Servant
entries.summary:
You are practiced in the routines of palaces, great houses, and other formal residences: service corridors, kitchens, chambers, schedules, household hierarchy, guest treatment, discreet access, protocol, and the quiet coordination required behind public grandeur.

Narrative effects: You notice who is served first, which entrance is used privately, whose instructions servants actually obey, and where formal household routine creates access or concealment.

entries.name: Pathfinder
entries.summary:
You are practiced at finding workable routes through difficult or unfamiliar terrain. Rather than merely knowing direction, you judge crossings, cover, gradients, footing, water, obstacles, exposure, concealment, and the signs left by previous travelers.

Narrative effects: You look beyond the obvious road for the route that best fits the group's actual needs: speed, safety, secrecy, footing, water, shelter, or ease of retreat.

entries.name: Potter
entries.summary:
You are professionally experienced at preparing clay, shaping vessels and objects, controlling thickness, drying, glazing, firing, repairing, and recognizing how heat and material quality affect finished ceramic work.

Narrative effects: You judge clay by touch, wall thickness by feel, drying by patience, and finished pieces by sound, surface, firing marks, cracks, and the maker's control.

entries.name: Prospector
entries.summary:
You are practiced at identifying potentially valuable ores, gems, stone, mineral traces, old workings, and natural signs that suggest a useful deposit. Your expertise combines recognizing material worth with reading the terrain that produced it.

Narrative effects: You examine weight, color, fracture, surrounding stone, old spoil, water stains, and previous digging before deciding whether a promising sample is actually worth pursuing.

entries.name: Mousefolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
Mousefolk Beastkin are kemonomimi-style beastkin with fully humanlike faces and bodies plus mouse ears, a thin tail, bright eyes, quick hands, and a small or slight humanlike build. They are not animal-headed, muzzled, furry-bodied, paw-handed, digitigrade animal-bodied, or full anthropomorphic animals.

Narrative effects: Sharp hearing, quick hands, and a slight humanlike build favor quiet movement and delicate manipulation. Nervousness, submissiveness, searching habits, or criminality are not inherent.

entries.name: Orc
entries.summary:
Orcs are large, robust mortal humanoids typically marked by powerful builds, broad features, pronounced tusks or tusk-like teeth, and a physiology capable of sustained physical exertion. Skin tones vary widely by lineage and region. Orcs are a people rather than a warrior profession: culture, upbringing, status, work, faith, and temperament come from their actual lives.

Narrative effects: Your size, tusks, and powerful frame can create an imposing first impression and support raw physical effort. Orc ancestry does not make you violent, militaristic, primitive, or culturally uniform.

entries.name: Otterfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
Otterfolk Beastkin are kemonomimi-style beastkin with fully humanlike faces and bodies plus otter ears, an otter tail, expressive face, water-ready posture, and quick playful movement. They are not animal-headed, muzzled, furry-bodied, paw-handed, digitigrade animal-bodied, or full anthropomorphic animals.

Narrative effects: A water-ready body, strong swimming instincts, and agile movement make currents and aquatic movement unusually natural. Playfulness and sociability are not required personality traits.

entries.name: Owlfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
Owlfolk Beastkin are kemonomimi-style beastkin with fully humanlike faces and bodies plus owl-like eyes, featherlike hair or markings, small ear tufts, and unusually still posture. They are not animal-headed, muzzled, furry-bodied, paw-handed, digitigrade animal-bodied, or full anthropomorphic animals.

Narrative effects: Night-adapted eyes, unusually still posture, and quiet movement favor observation and tracking in dim conditions. Scholarly interests are cultural or personal, not biologically required.

entries.name: Pantherfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
Pantherfolk Beastkin are kemonomimi-style beastkin with fully humanlike faces and bodies plus panther ears, a tail, dark hair or markings, low smooth movement, and eyes that catch dim light. They are not animal-headed, muzzled, furry-bodied, paw-handed, digitigrade animal-bodied, or full anthropomorphic animals.

Narrative effects: Low, smooth movement, strong balance, and eyes adapted to dim light make pantherfolk exceptionally suited to moving quietly and following prey or threats. Do not impose a violent or solitary temperament.

entries.name: Misdirector
entries.summary:
You are practiced at steering attention away from what matters through selective truth, implication, distraction, and carefully chosen emphasis. You read what people are looking for, then give them something else convincing to follow.

Narrative effects: You notice where attention is pointed and instinctively consider how to redirect it.

entries.name: Negotiator
entries.summary:
You are practiced at reaching workable agreements through concessions, leverage, timing, and clear terms. You know how to identify what each side can give, what each side actually needs, and where a proposal can be reshaped without assuming a particular profession or social rank.

Narrative effects: You naturally listen for the point where wants, limits, and possible concessions overlap.

entries.name: People Reader
entries.summary:
You are skilled at reading tone, posture, hesitation, emotion, contradiction, motive, and interpersonal tension. You notice what people feel and how those feelings fit the social situation without automatically knowing hidden thoughts or objective truth.

Narrative effects: You watch the difference between what someone says, what they feel, and how everyone around them reacts.

entries.name: Performer
entries.summary:
You are an experienced general performer who can hold attention through acting, recitation, movement, entertainment, staged emotion, or public presentation. Performance can create convincing appearances and distractions, but it does not automatically make every audience receptive.

Narrative effects: You understand how timing, expression, and deliberate presentation change what an audience notices and feels.

entries.name: Persuasive Speaker
entries.summary:
You are skilled at changing minds through clear reasoning, sincerity, emotional appeal, patient explanation, and confident delivery. Persuasion creates a stronger case; it never guarantees agreement where interests, evidence, values, or trust run against you.

Narrative effects: You try to understand what matters to someone before deciding which argument they might actually hear.

entries.name: Playful Tease
entries.summary:
You are practiced at playful flirting built through banter, teasing, ambiguity, feigned innocence, and light misdirection. The technique relies on mutual engagement and does not turn manipulation, persistence, or ignored boundaries into successful courtship.

Narrative effects: You know how to leave just enough unsaid for mutual interest to become part of the conversation.

entries.name: Pressure Bargainer
entries.summary:
You are skilled at bargaining from a position of firmness, pressure, and controlled refusal. You can hold a line, make costs feel immediate, and push for better terms without turning every negotiation into a threat or assuming that you are cruel.

Narrative effects: When terms become unfavorable, you know how to make the other side feel the cost of refusing you.

entries.name: Protocol Navigator
entries.summary:
You are practiced at navigating formal procedures of approach: introductions, audiences, invitations, precedence, official meetings, institutional hierarchy, and ceremonial access. You know who should speak first, who must be acknowledged, and which social route is most likely to open a door.

Narrative effects: You read a formal room as a sequence of permissions, roles, witnesses, and expected approaches.

entries.name: Provocateur
entries.summary:
You can bait, challenge, unsettle, and deliberately push emotional pressure points to encourage mistakes or premature reactions. Provocation creates risk as well as opportunity, and a target may respond with anger, withdrawal, suspicion, or retaliation.

Narrative effects: You know how to make a carefully chosen remark feel harder to ignore than it deserves.

entries.name: Mage Attire Set
entries.summary: Clothing suited for spellcasters: layered, flexible, and arranged to leave hands and focus tools free. It marks the wearer as someone expected to work with mana.

entries.name: Merchant's Fine Clothes Set
entries.summary: Respectable, well-made clothing that signals prosperity without claiming noble blood. Suitable for counting houses, trade meetings, guild halls, and caravan patrons.

entries.name: Military Uniform Set
entries.summary: A uniform suited for militia, army service, border duty, or martial training. It is not armor by itself, but it announces discipline and chain of command.

entries.name: Mining Workwear Set
entries.summary: Rugged clothing suited for tunnels, stone dust, mud, darkness, and heavy labor below ground. It is made for function before comfort.

entries.name: Monastic Robes Set
entries.summary: Simple robes suited for monasteries, meditation halls, secluded study, restraint, and disciplined living. They carry little ornament and much intention.

entries.name: Mountain Travel Clothes Set
entries.summary: Sturdy layered clothing suited for slopes, cold mornings, rough stone, high passes, wind, and mountain settlements.

entries.name: Mourning Clothes Set
entries.summary: Somber clothing suited for funerals, grief rites, memorials, and households marked by recent loss. It carries quiet social meaning wherever mourning is understood.

entries.name: Noble's Attire Set
entries.summary: Fine clothing suited to noble birth, inheritance, or high household standing. The cut, fabric, and details announce that the wearer was raised near privilege.

entries.name: Nomad Caravan Clothes Set
entries.summary: Layered, mobile clothing suited for caravan life, long roads, changing weather, dust, trade camps, and people who carry home with them.

entries.name: Palace Servant Livery Set
entries.summary: Formal servant livery suitable for a palace, noble estate, or high household. Better made than common service clothes, but still meant to identify the wearer as staff.

entries.name: Peasant's Work Clothes Set
entries.summary: Rough, durable clothing made for fields, barns, muddy roads, and hard labor. It speaks of practical survival rather than status.

entries.name: Performer Costume Set
entries.summary: Expressive clothing suited for stage work, street performance, festivals, taverns, dances, and dramatic entrances. It is made to be noticed.

entries.name: Mage Ward Garments Set
entries.summary: Protective garments designed for spellcasters, woven or prepared to help resist minor magical strain, sparks, backlash, or hostile energy without functioning like true armor.

entries.name: No Armor
entries.summary: You begin without armor or protective gear. Whether by poverty, confidence, magical preference, social circumstance, or simple bad luck, you rely on clothing, movement, and whatever protection you can find later.

entries.name: Padded Armor Set
entries.summary: A basic padded armor set made from layered cloth, batting, and stitched protection. It is humble, inexpensive, and better than facing blades in ordinary clothes.

entries.name: Plate Armor Set
entries.summary: A full or near-full plate armor set of shaped metal pieces, fitted straps, padding, and reinforced joints. Expensive, prestigious, and highly protective when properly worn.

entries.name: Mace
entries.summary: A heavy single-handed bludgeon designed to crush armor and bone alike, bypassing the protection that turns edged weapons aside.

entries.name: Mage Staff
entries.summary: A staff designed as a magical focus and walking implement, suited for channeling mana through deliberate gestures and stable posture. It favors steady casting, ritual positioning, and controlled output over quick portability. Less a sidearm than a declaration that the wielder expects magic to answer.

entries.name: Main-Gauche
entries.summary: Starting weapon for Dueling. A parrying dagger used with precision blades to t.

entries.name: Maul
entries.summary: A two-handed crushing weapon that sacrifices speed for overwhelming impact and armor-breaking force.

entries.name: Odachi
entries.summary: Starting weapon for Heavy Blades. An exceptionally long two-handed curved blade, la.

entries.name: Parrying Sword
entries.summary: A narrow defensive blade used to bind, deflect, and answer with precise counter-thrusts.

entries.name: Partisan
entries.summary: A spear-like polearm with side lugs that supports thrusting, binding, and defensive reach control.

entries.name: Pike
entries.summary: An extremely long formation spear meant to stop charges, dominate lanes, and punish enemies before they close.

entries.name: Made a Powerful Enemy
entries.summary:
Through conflict, refusal, accident, competition, insult, exposure, or some other event, you gained the hostility of someone with significantly more influence or resources than you.

Narrative effects: You learned to function despite intimidation and to pay attention to the relationships and influence surrounding a dangerous opponent.

entries.name: Magic Hidden from Authorities
entries.summary:
For a period, you concealed magical activity, talent, study, or suspicion from authorities who might have regulated, punished, recruited, or investigated you.

Narrative effects: You learned how institutions watch for forbidden or regulated behavior and how to conceal information from them.

entries.name: Magic Suppressed by Family
entries.summary:
Your family or household discouraged, concealed, restricted, or outright forbade your magical interests or development.

Narrative effects: You learned to control outward reactions and conceal interests when people close to you disapproved. This does not determine why they opposed magic.

entries.name: Mana Awakening Crisis
entries.summary:
A sudden period of magical instability, uncontrolled mana, or frightening magical sensitivity disrupted your teenage life and demanded attention.

Narrative effects: The crisis taught you that magical power requires control and understanding. It does not itself grant an Arcana or increased mana.

entries.name: Ordinary Teen Until It Happened
entries.summary:
Your teenage life had been comparatively ordinary until one unexpected event disrupted it. The specific event should come from the established background, Story Start, or character history rather than being invented automatically.

Narrative effects: You retain a strong grounding in ordinary life while having learned that circumstances can change abruptly. Do not invent hidden destiny, ancestry, or catastrophe to explain this trait.

entries.name: Patron Lost Interest
entries.summary:
Someone who had sponsored, encouraged, recommended, financed, or promoted you lost interest before your future was secure.

Narrative effects: Losing support taught you both how patronage works socially and how difficult it can be to regain someone's confidence.

entries.name: Protected Younger Street Kids
entries.summary:
You became one of the older youths who protected younger street children from bullies, predatory adults, gangs, guards, or other dangers.

Narrative effects: You learned to fight when necessary and to become someone younger people looked toward when trouble appeared.

entries.name: Public Duel Disgraced
entries.summary:
A duel, spar, tournament bout, or public challenge ended in embarrassment through defeat, misconduct, panic, cheating accusations, or another humiliating outcome.

Narrative effects: You learned that public combat involves reputation and expected conduct as well as technical fighting ability.

entries.name: Public Failure
entries.summary:
You failed at something important while enough people were watching for the embarrassment to become part of your reputation or self-image.

Narrative effects: Public failure taught you how difficult it can be to perform under observation and how much courage returning to the same audience can require.

entries.name: Market Stall Worker
entries.summary:
You spent adolescence selling goods from a stall or market space, negotiating with customers, arranging stock, judging merchandise, and learning what people would actually pay.

Narrative effects: Direct trade became a practiced skill, supported by a strong eye for the value and quality of physical goods.

entries.name: Mercenary Trainee
entries.summary:
You trained under professional fighters, hired guards, caravan blades, sellswords, or another group that valued practical violence over ceremony or prestige.

Narrative effects: You developed a direct, forceful martial foundation built around practical one-handed weapons commonly suited to hard fighting.

entries.name: Merchant Negotiator
entries.summary:
You began taking an active role in commercial negotiation rather than merely watching adults trade. Prices, terms, quantities, delivery conditions, and customer relationships became your responsibility.

Narrative effects: You became a practiced negotiator who understands both exchange terms and the importance of getting another person to accept them.

entries.name: Messenger Teen
entries.summary:
You worked regularly carrying messages, parcels, instructions, or news across a settlement or between nearby communities where speed and knowing the route directly affected your usefulness.

Narrative effects: Route-finding became a major practical skill supported by years of moving quickly between destinations.

entries.name: Militia Teen
entries.summary:
You trained with a local militia, levy, town defense group, village muster, or other part-time defensive force. Formation drills and practical weapons mattered more than elegance.

Narrative effects: You developed a practical spear-and-shield foundation suited to organized common defense.

entries.name: Miller's Apprentice
entries.summary:
You trained around a working mill, learning its mechanisms, maintenance, material flow, heavy sacks, safety, and the practical problems caused when machinery stopped.

Narrative effects: Mill mechanisms became deeply familiar, alongside the physical work required to keep material moving through them.

entries.name: Monastery Student
entries.summary:
Your adolescence followed the structured life of a monastery or similarly disciplined religious community, balancing study, work, contemplation, and religious instruction.

Narrative effects: Routine, contemplation, and religious study became deeply familiar regardless of whether you maintained the same beliefs later.

entries.name: Monster-Hunter Trainee
entries.summary:
You trained under people who hunted dangerous creatures, learning that distance, preparation, reach, and knowing when not to close with a monster could matter more than heroics.

Narrative effects: You developed practical combat habits for dangerous creatures using strong ranged attacks and reach weapons without automatically becoming an expert monster scholar.

entries.name: Mounted Guard Trainee
entries.summary:
You trained for mounted protective or military work, learning to strike from horseback and remain effective when a charge became close combat.

Narrative effects: Lance fighting became your primary martial foundation, supported by training with heavier blades for combat after closing.

entries.name: No Clear Path
entries.summary:
You moved between casual work, lessons, hobbies, family expectations, temporary opportunities, and periods of uncertainty without one direction becoming clearly dominant during adolescence.

Narrative effects: Trying several directions made you attentive to how other people organize their lives and gave you broad familiarity with ordinary social possibilities. This path does not imply failure or lack of ability.

entries.name: Noble Page
entries.summary:
You served as a page within a noble household or court, carrying messages, attending important people, learning rank, observing ceremonies, and being expected to behave correctly.

Narrative effects: Formal noble service gave you strong etiquette and practical familiarity with heraldic identity and rank.

entries.name: Palace Guard Cadet
entries.summary:
You entered early training connected to a palace guard, royal household guard, elite estate guard, or similarly prestigious protective force. Discipline and reliable armed presence mattered as much as appearance.

Narrative effects: You received sustained training in a strong defensive fighting style associated with guarding important people and places.

entries.name: Performer in Training
entries.summary:
You trained seriously in acting, storytelling, dance, comedy, recitation, stagecraft, or another form of public performance rather than treating it as a casual hobby.

Narrative effects: You became comfortable holding an audience's attention and learned how presentation can influence how people respond.

entries.name: Pickpocket Crew Member
entries.summary:
You worked with youths or adults who stole from pockets, bags, belts, crowded stalls, or distracted travelers, often relying on teamwork rather than acting alone.

Narrative effects: Quick hands and remaining unobtrusive in crowded environments became sustained practical skills.

entries.name: Potter's Apprentice
entries.summary:
You trained in preparing clay, shaping vessels, controlling thickness, drying, glazing, firing, repairing mistakes, and judging material through your hands.

Narrative effects: Clay work became a serious practical skill, and you developed exceptional familiarity with materials through touch.

entries.name: Mana-Sensitive Infant
entries.summary:
As an infant or toddler, you reacted to mana: crying near unstable spells, calming near gentle magic, reaching for enchanted objects, or unsettling casters who noticed too much awareness in you.

Narrative effects: You feel unstable mana like pressure in the air before others notice anything wrong.

entries.name: Marked by an Old Scar
entries.summary:
You carry a scar from your toddler years: accident, illness, beast, blade, fire, fall, ritual, or something no one fully explained. It is old now, but still part of your story.

Narrative effects: You touch or hide an old scar when old fear, old pain, or old questions rise.

entries.name: Military Cradle
entries.summary:
You spent your toddler years around barracks, forts, officers, drill yards, uniforms, watch rotations, or military households. Discipline entered your life before you had words for it.

Narrative effects: You respond quickly to shouted orders, alarm bells, and the sound of boots moving together.

entries.name: Monastery Cradle
entries.summary:
You spent your earliest years in a monastery or disciplined retreat, surrounded by routine, silence, simple meals, meditation, work, prayer, or study.

Narrative effects: You become calm around repetition, quiet halls, and simple routines.

entries.name: Monster Quieted Near You
entries.summary:
A beast, monster, or dangerous creature once grew strangely calm near you when you were very young. This does not mean you control monsters, but the story left people uneasy or amazed.

Narrative effects: You are slower to panic around strange creatures than most people think is sensible.

entries.name: Moved Under False Papers
entries.summary:
As a toddler, you were moved between places under forged, borrowed, altered, or deliberately misleading papers. You may not have understood any of it at the time, but false names, invented relationships, or misleading records became part of your earliest history.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable with the idea that documents and official stories can be constructed to hide where a child came from. This trait does not define who created the false papers or why unless another part of the story does.

entries.name: Nearly Drowned
entries.summary:
You nearly drowned as a very young child and survived through rescue, luck, instinct, or desperate intervention. Water became part of your earliest story as something both ordinary and dangerous.

Narrative effects: You respect deep water and are less likely to freeze when forced to act in it, though the event need not have left you fearless.

entries.name: Neglected Child
entries.summary:
You were not always harmed directly, but you were overlooked, underfed, left waiting, or treated as something inconvenient. You learned early that being quiet could be safer than needing too much.

Narrative effects: You notice who is ignored in a room, because you know how that feels.

entries.name: Only Child Then
entries.summary:
For your earliest years, you were the only young child in the household or the only child receiving close day-to-day attention. Adults had fewer children to divide their attention between, and your first social world was shaped more by older people than by siblings.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable around adults and familiar with being expected to entertain yourself when no other children are present.

entries.name: Parent Returned After an Absence
entries.summary:
A parent or primary caregiver who had been absent returned while you were still very young. Their return changed the household again, whether it brought relief, confusion, resentment, affection, or a difficult adjustment.

Narrative effects: You pay attention to the gap between who someone remembers a person being and who that person has become after time apart.

entries.name: Passed Between Caregivers
entries.summary:
Responsibility for you shifted repeatedly between relatives, guardians, households, institutions, or temporary caretakers. No single pair of hands defined your entire toddlerhood.

Narrative effects: You adapt quickly to different household expectations and notice how care changes from one person or community to another.

entries.name: Protected by Older Sibling
entries.summary:
An older sibling, cousin, wardmate, or older child protected you when you were small. Their presence shaped your first idea of safety, loyalty, and what it means to stand between danger and someone smaller.

Narrative effects: You look for the person quietly shielding others, even when no one thanks them.

entries.name: Never Sat Still
entries.summary:
You climbed, ran, crawled, spun, bounced, fidgeted, explored, and turned every quiet moment into an excuse to move.

Narrative effects: You think well while moving and become restless when forced into prolonged inactivity.

entries.name: Noticed Missing Things
entries.summary:
You reacted when a familiar toy vanished, a cup moved, someone's usual object was absent, or a room no longer looked the way you expected.

Narrative effects: Absence and small changes in familiar arrangements stand out strongly to you.

entries.name: Patient With Puzzles
entries.summary:
Simple puzzles, shapes, knots, hidden objects, fitting games, and problems that frustrated other children could hold your attention for surprisingly long periods.

Narrative effects: When a problem looks solvable, you are unusually willing to keep examining it rather than immediately giving up.

entries.name: Played with Water
entries.summary:
Basins, puddles, streams, baths, rain barrels, cups, and anything containing water became immediate invitations to splash, pour, stir, touch, or climb into it.

Narrative effects: You are physically comfortable around water and attentive to how it moves and feels. This temperament does not imply Water Arcana.

entries.name: Marksmanship Practice
entries.summary:
You deliberately trained ranged precision with bows, learning controlled release, distance judgment, sight picture, and maintaining aim under distraction. Grants +2 Accuracy and +1 Perception.

Narrative effects: You judge distance, movement, line of sight, and your own breathing before committing to a precise shot.

entries.name: Meditative Practice
entries.summary:
You trained breath, posture, attention, emotional regulation, and deliberate stillness through meditation, martial forms, religious practice, or another disciplined contemplative routine. Grants +2 Willpower and +1 Perception.

Narrative effects: When pressure rises, you instinctively steady your breathing and create a moment of internal distance before deciding how to respond.

entries.name: Negotiation Practice
entries.summary:
You practiced reaching workable terms through price, leverage, compromise, persuasion, and careful attention to what each side actually values. Grants +2 Communication and +1 Intelligence.

Narrative effects: You listen for priorities, hidden costs, walk-away points, and where changing the terms may matter more than arguing harder.

entries.name: Nimble Training
entries.summary:
You trained balance, footwork, reflexes, and whole-body control through movement drills, dance, obstacle work, scouting, games, or repeated practice in awkward spaces. Grants +2 Dexterity and +1 Fighting.

Narrative effects: You rarely stand flat-footed; your weight stays ready to shift, turn, duck, accelerate, or recover from a bad step.

entries.name: Precision Drills
entries.summary:
You trained fine visual-motor precision without tying that discipline to one weapon, practicing exact placement, steady hands, and careful correction. Grants +2 Accuracy and +1 Willpower.

Narrative effects: You slow down when precision matters, steady unnecessary movement, and make deliberate micro-adjustments rather than forcing a rushed result.

entries.name: Public Speaking Drills
entries.summary:
You trained to speak while watched, learning projection, pacing, emphasis, audience awareness, and how to continue when nerves or interruption would derail an unpracticed speaker. Grants +2 Communication and +1 Willpower.

Narrative effects: You instinctively shape volume, rhythm, pauses, and emphasis to keep a group following what you are saying.

entries.name: Market District
entries.summary:
You grew up amid stalls, carts, vendors, customers, deliveries, shouting, shortages, bargains, street food, crowds, petty arguments, local news, and constant movement of goods and people.

Narrative effects: You understand everyday negotiation and are comfortable following rumors, questions, and social threads through busy public spaces.

entries.name: Merchant Household
entries.summary:
You were raised around trade goods, haggling, suppliers, customers, caravan news, risk, debt, stock, and opportunity. Household conversations regularly concerned what things cost and what people would actually pay.

Narrative effects: You understand negotiation and material value without automatically inheriting wealth, a business, or merchant status.

entries.name: Military Household
entries.summary:
Soldiers, guards, officers, quartermasters, veterans, or military retainers dominated the household that raised you. Orders, schedules, equipment, deployments, inspections, and discussions of duty were part of ordinary life.

Narrative effects: You understand military routines and disciplined behavior without automatically possessing combat training or command authority.

entries.name: Miller's Household
entries.summary:
You grew up around a working mill where grain, sacks, gears, belts, stones, waterwheels, wind mechanisms, customers, maintenance, and heavy loads were part of everyday life.

Narrative effects: You understand basic mechanical systems and are accustomed to the physical work involved in moving heavy materials.

entries.name: Mining Town
entries.summary:
You were raised in a settlement shaped by mines, tunnels, lifts, supports, carts, ore processing, dust, shift changes, machinery, and the constant awareness that stone can become dangerous.

Narrative effects: You understand basic constructed systems used around mines and are accustomed to paying attention to echoes, machinery, cracking, and other important sounds.

entries.name: Monastery Raised
entries.summary:
You spent much of childhood in a monastery, secluded religious community, contemplative order, or disciplined spiritual household. Repetition, quiet work, study, ritual, restraint, and communal schedules shaped everyday life.

Narrative effects: You understand disciplined routine and religious practice whether you remained devout, became doubtful, or eventually left.

entries.name: Mountain Hold
entries.summary:
You grew up in a mountain settlement, cliff community, high valley, remote hold, or similarly steep environment where elevation, difficult paths, severe weather, and exposed terrain shaped ordinary movement.

Narrative effects: You are accustomed to vertical terrain and genuine physical exposure to cold, wind, altitude, and difficult conditions.

entries.name: Noble Among Commoners
entries.summary:
You possessed noble birth, noble connection, or a recognized high-status background while spending much of your upbringing among ordinary people. Daily life exposed you to assumptions and routines very different from those your status might otherwise have prescribed.

Narrative effects: You are accustomed to moving between social expectations and noticing when rank changes how the same person or action is interpreted.

entries.name: Noble Hostage Ward
entries.summary:
You spent formative years as a politically important ward in another household, court, estate, or allied community. You may have been treated kindly, coldly, ceremonially, or as leverage, but your presence carried implications beyond ordinary fostering.

Narrative effects: You understand how hospitality, obligation, alliance, leverage, and formal courtesy can coexist within the same political arrangement.

entries.name: Nomad Caravan
entries.summary:
Your household or community moved regularly rather than remaining in one permanent settlement. Routes, camps, animals, weather, landmarks, seasonal destinations, packing, and departure were ordinary parts of life.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable orienting yourself across long routes and controlling mounts during ordinary travel.

entries.name: Orchard Estate
entries.summary:
You were raised around orchards, vineyards, groves, gardens, seasonal workers, pruning, harvest, storage, preserving, fermentation, weather, and crops whose value depended on years of careful cultivation.

Narrative effects: You understand cultivated plants and possess practical familiarity with preserving, fermenting, or preparing the products of a harvest.

entries.name: Orphaned Ward
entries.summary:
You grew up as a ward without parents serving as your primary caregivers. An orphanage, household, temple, local authority, charity, institution, or rotating caregivers may have been responsible for you.

Narrative effects: You are accustomed to living among people with different needs and to making your case to caregivers, officials, older children, or others controlling limited choices.

entries.name: Pilgrim Hostel
entries.summary:
You were raised at a hostel, hospice, shrine lodging, or other place serving people traveling for religious reasons. Guests arrived from many communities carrying different customs, stories, needs, and interpretations of shared faith.

Narrative effects: You understand religious travel and are familiar with how customs and interpretations vary between communities.
